panels.title: Sources OK / total
panels.description: Two counts from the last cycle: sources that returned a usable body, and sources configured. Neither is a health reading on its own — a source dropping out shows here as ok falling below total, and whether that cost anything is the kept count to the left. Colour therefore carries no health direction here: every value from 0 up is painted in the plain text colour, and the only coloured state is red for no data. That base step is deliberate, not decoration. A stat that declares no thresholds does NOT render neutral — Grafana merges the standard field-config default into it, a green base with red from 80 — so before 2026-08-08 this tile painted an absent series GREEN, and painted a real count RED only once it reached 80. Both counts sat in the hundreds for all but 81 of the 20578 sample-minutes in the 15d window ending 2026-08-08 19:30Z — total never fell below 164, and ok was at or above 100 in 20497 of those 20578, 99.61% of them — but in those 81 minutes, 2026-07-26 19:59–21:19Z, ok sat at exactly 1, so the old tile painted the worst source outage in the window GREEN beside a RED total. Read as an INSTANT query: if the gauges are not being exported right now the tile reads NO SOURCE COUNTS on red, whatever the dashboard time range holds — writeMetrics returns before both of them while m.last is nil, so that is every restart before the first published cycle.

panels.title: Last publish age
panels.description: Time since the last cycle that PUBLISHED a list. A cycle that runs and fails does not reset it — Metrics.Observe sets the timestamp, ObserveError does not — so this answers "how stale is /stable.txt", not "when did the worker last run"; for that read cycles/h on the cycle panel. Read as an INSTANT query: if stable_last_success_timestamp_seconds is not being exported right now the tile reads NO PUBLISH TIMESTAMP on red, whatever the dashboard time range holds. Three causes, and this tile cannot tell them apart: the process restarted and has not published yet (writeMetrics returns before every gauge while m.last is nil), the scrape is failing, or the worker is gone. cycles/h separates the first from the rest.

panels.title: Pipeline funnel
panels.description: Four counts from the last cycle, listed here in pipeline order (the legend runs in target order: merged, probed, dead-skipped, kept). merged = unique nodes after dedupe; dead-skipped = nodes never probed because a recent probe found them dead; probed = nodes latency-probed; kept = nodes published. merged = dead-skipped + probed, so the gap between the merged and probed lines is entirely the dead cache and is not loss. The drop from probed to kept is the latency probe plus the through-node gates.

panels.title: Through-node filter drops by reason
panels.description: blocked = the service answered but refused this egress; unreachable = the request never completed through the node (it still passed the latency probe, so this is the service refusing at the CDN or the node failing on real traffic); slow = below the bandwidth filter minimum. A gate that RAN and dropped nobody IS here, at zero: apiFilter.apply and bandwidthFilter.apply each assign a fully populated Dropped map on the path that completes — {blocked, unreachable} and {slow, unreachable}, both keys, zero-valued or not — so it emits zero-valued samples; chatgpt/blocked and tidal/blocked were both 0 in the cycle published 2026-08-08 18:26Z, beside chatgpt/unreachable 8 and tidal/unreachable 2. A gate that emits NOTHING never reached that assignment: apiFilter's three early returns (enabled() false — configured but with no usable key; nil outcomes; context cancelled mid-check) and bandwidthFilter's two (nil outcomes, cancelled context) all keep the EMPTY Dropped map the FilterReport was initialised with, and writeFilters iterates sortedKeys(Dropped), so no drop sample is written at all — while filter_in/filter_kept still are, on the in-vs-kept panel. Absence therefore means INERT, a present zero means RAN CLEAN, and this panel does separate them. A gate absent from `filters:` is a third state: it emits nothing NEW on either panel, but the rows it already wrote do not disappear, they stop. gemini was commented out on 2026-08-08 and its last sample is 05:26:03Z, so it still draws blocked and unreachable lines ending there on any range reaching back that far — as this dashboard's own now-24h default still did at 2026-08-08 19:30Z. The legend reduces with `last`, not `lastNotNull`: a gate that stops mid-window leaves its legend cell empty rather than freezing at the last healthy value it published.

panels.title: Top source groups: channels folded, everything else as-is (last cycle)

targets.expr: sum by (channel) (label_replace(label_replace(stable_source_nodes_total{job="$job"}, "channel", "$1", "source", "^(.*)$"), "channel", "$1", "source", "^(tg-[a-z0-9-]+)-[0-9a-f]{6}$")) and on(channel) topk(25, sum by (channel) (label_replace(label_replace(stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}, "channel", "$1", "source", "^(.*)$"), "channel", "$1", "source", "^(tg-[a-z0-9-]+)-[0-9a-f]{6}$")))

sum by (channel) (label_replace(label_replace(stable_source_tested_nodes{job="$job"}, "channel", "$1", "source", "^(.*)$"), "channel", "$1", "source", "^(tg-[a-z0-9-]+)-[0-9a-f]{6}$")) and on(channel) topk(25, sum by (channel) (label_replace(label_replace(stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}, "channel", "$1", "source", "^(.*)$"), "channel", "$1", "source", "^(tg-[a-z0-9-]+)-[0-9a-f]{6}$")))

sum by (channel) (label_replace(label_replace(stable_source_published_nodes{job="$job"}, "channel", "$1", "source", "^(.*)$"), "channel", "$1", "source", "^(tg-[a-z0-9-]+)-[0-9a-f]{6}$")) and on(channel) topk(25, sum by (channel) (label_replace(label_replace(stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}, "channel", "$1", "source", "^(.*)$"), "channel", "$1", "source", "^(tg-[a-z0-9-]+)-[0-9a-f]{6}$")))

panels.description: Same four counts as the per-source table, but summed by GROUP, for the top 25 groups ranked on valid — the column this table is also sorted by, so adding columns never reorders it. A group is derived from the source name by stripping the -<sha6> suffix that sourceName appends per URL, so tg-genliberty-7e9b21 and its 16 siblings collapse into one tg-genliberty row. Nearly every source the crawler writes into config/private.yaml carries a channel-attributed tg-<slug>-<sha6> name; a handful of channels supply dozens of URLs each while many carry exactly one, and the curated git-tracked config/sources.yaml contributes further names that carry no channel at all. That mix is why this column keeps the tg- prefix where panel 8 strips it: there the query fixes the owner, so the prefix carries nothing (panel 22 has nothing to strip - its rows never carry one), while here managed and curated names share one bucket space and the prefix is all that tells them apart. The header reads group, not channel, because the buckets are not all channels: measured on :3020, host clock 2026-08-17 04:33 +03:00, the query bucketed 493 reporting sources into 108 groups - 61 folded channels, tg-inline and the legacy tg-96c4d7c7a7 which fold nothing and are no channel, and 45 curated names - and the top 25 it drew held 18 channels beside 7 curated names. For the live configured total read panel 3 (Sources OK / total, stable_sources_total) at the top of this dashboard rather than any figure quoted here — the crawler rewrites private.yaml hourly, and that gauge reflects the config the last cycle loaded, so it trails the file on disk by a cycle. As one dated illustration, the cycle published 2026-08-15 17:09Z: the 350 private plus 46 curated names it loaded — 396, exactly what stable_sources_total read — produce 94 buckets, 45 of them channels of which 25 hold more than one URL, and 87 buckets reported a series, of which this table shows the top 25. The 25th row was tg-96c4d7c7a7 at 1007 valid, so 62 reporting buckets sat below that cutoff and drew nothing: a channel you cannot find here is under the cutoff far more often than it is absent from the config. Every config figure below is that loaded config rather than the file on disk, and is stamped to the cycle rather than to the day for a reason: the crawler rewrote private.yaml to 357 names at 17:20Z, eleven minutes later. Fan-out does not decide placement — the per-URL distribution does. tg-file-vpn-2 had the second-largest fan-out in that config (42 URLs, all cyb-portal.com/CP-0NN) and placed six rows in the crawler-managed per-URL top 25, but not because its URLs are interchangeable: on that cycle their valid ran 2669, 2217, 2051, 1975, 1627, 1500 and then fell away through a median of 222 to a tail of 15, 2 and 0, so only SIX cleared that table's top-25 cutoff of 1185 while the other 36 placed nowhere. That cutoff is the crawler-managed one because panel 8 ranks source=~"tg-.*" only: on the same 17:09Z cycle the six curated names that had held both-owner top-25 slots (bywarm-merged, fifthidea, etoneyaproject, goida, flat447, kasesm) rank in the hand-curated table instead, and 25th place falls from 1970 to 1185. tg-dailyv2ry is the case this panel exists for: 71 URLs on bin.mudfish.net, best single URL 182 valid, so not one of its rows reaches the per-URL table, yet it sums to 9339 and ranks 7th here. Skew, not count, is the point: a channel earns per-URL rows only when a few of its links are individually large, and when none are, this table is the only place its weight shows at all. Whether a channel's many names are one panel or many is decided by what they return, not by how their URLs look. Fetched 17:27Z the same day with the worker's own UA: eight of tg-holost-vpn's URLs sit at eight DIFFERENT raw.githubusercontent.com repo paths (Ai123999/1Mond, 2Tues, 3Wend, 4Thur, 5Frid, 6Satu, 7Sand and RU_other) yet answer byte-identical — md5 2193975ecadf359d136da4658ca7a1e6, 121 endpoints each, pairwise Jaccard 1.000 — so eight unrelated-looking paths are one panel, and across all ten Ai123999 URLs 1520 endpoints collapse to a union of 636, 41.8% distinct. A 12-URL sample of tg-dailyv2ry the same day ran the other way, mean pairwise Jaccard 0.054 and 74.5% distinct, so those names really are separate panels. Nothing about the hosts or the paths tells the two cases apart; only the fetched payload does. Attribution is first-seen-channel-wins and keeps the URL verbatim — private.yaml's url: entries carry zero duplicate URLs, all 349 of them on that cycle — so the framing above, one channel publishing many URLs, has a mirror: when several channels relay ONE panel, the rows split across them. In that cycle's config, 47 names differing only in ?payload= on a single is.wepogp.gay path sat under tg-hiddifycode, tg-o00000000i and tg-v2raytunsub — by 17:20Z the crawler had made it 49. There is no resource rollup to add here, because a host is not a resource key. In the bucket space this table actually renders — curated names included, since the inner label_replace gives every name matching neither strip pattern a bucket of its own — raw.githubusercontent.com sat under 62 of that cycle's 87 reporting buckets: 28 private buckets, one of them the channel-less tg-96c4d7c7a7, plus 34 of config/sources.yaml's 46 curated names. Over private.yaml alone it is those 28 buckets, or 27 channels once tg-96c4d7c7a7 is set aside, but 62 is the figure for what you actually see drawn. Either way one host spans dozens of unrelated panels while, per Ai123999 above, also hiding eight names behind a single one — and the full URL is exactly the per-URL table. Names matching neither strip pattern form their own single-URL buckets, per-URL numbers unchanged: commsub, the only hand-named entry in private.yaml; tg-inline, the inline-harvest source, which carries body: instead of url:; and the legacy tg-<10hex> form tg-96c4d7c7a7, which carries no channel. fifthidea, bywarm-merged and goida are NOT private — they are curated entries in git-tracked config/sources.yaml, as are the 43 other names there. Column meanings are exactly the per-source table's, and so are its caveats plus one more: valid is counted BEFORE merge dedupes, so summing it over a channel's URLs also counts every node that several of that channel's own URLs carry — globally sum(stable_source_valid_nodes{job="$job"}) / scalar(stable_merged_nodes{job="$job"}) was 5.76 on the 2026-08-15 17:09Z cycle, and within a channel whose names sit behind one panel the overlap is far worse, so channel valid reads as an upper bound. filtered does NOT inflate: merge leaves exactly one <source>-NNN label per published node, so sum(stable_source_published_nodes) == stable_kept_nodes exactly (172 == 172 on that cycle) and summing it by channel stays exact. Use the per-URL table, not this one, to retire a single dead link: the dead-node cache, the dedupe and the attribution all key on the individual URL, and only its own row tells you which of a channel's 71 links went dark.

panels.title: Top sources: crawler-managed (last cycle)
panels.description:
Four counts per CRAWLER-MANAGED source (source=~"tg-.*") from the last cycle, in pipeline order, for the top 25 of that set ranked on valid — the column this table is also sorted by, so adding columns never reorders it. yielded = raw nodes the source yielded; valid = what survived the IP-stage filters, counted per source BEFORE merge dedupes across sources; kept = that source's nodes that survived the URL test, counted after merge; filtered = what then passed every through-node gate and reached the published payload. valid >= kept >= filtered holds, but the first gap is NOT probe failure alone: valid is pre-merge and kept is post-merge, so valid - kept also absorbs every node whose server:port another source supplied first (merge keeps the first label and drops the rest) plus the dead-node cache skip. That dedupe term dominates — sum(stable_source_valid_nodes) / scalar(stable_merged_nodes) ran 1.00–4.93 (avg 3.37) over the 15d window ending 2026-08-08 19:30Z, across both owners. filtered DOES attribute published nodes to a source, exactly one per node, because merge leaves one <source>-NNN label per duplicate group: a large valid with filtered 0 means nothing reached the payload under that source's own name, whether the nodes were duplicates, dead-cached, probe failures or gate drops. Note the vocabulary: kept here is THIS table's column name for the probe verdict, while the global stable_kept_nodes gauge counts what this table calls filtered.

The displayed name has its tg- prefix stripped by an outermost label_replace(<expr>, "source", "$1", "source", "tg-(.*)") applied identically in all four targets. That is display-only PromQL and it changes no source NAME: the prefix stays in the name and remains WRITE AUTHORITY over config/private.yaml — crawl.go:367 rechecks only prefixed sources, :419 preserves non-prefixed entries verbatim, and :546 counts only prefixed ones so bulk-prune can never delete a hand-added source. The and on(source) join sits INSIDE the label_replace, so it matches the ORIGINAL prefixed name; the joinByField transformation does not — Prometheus returns frames whose source label is already rewritten, so joinByField matches the STRIPPED name and the original name never reaches Grafana at all. The join is still correct because all four targets rewrite identically and the strip is injective over every name that can reach this table, so the stripped key is as unique as the original — the 439 tg- sources reporting series on :9091, job sub-preprocessor, 2026-08-16 12:45 +03:00 strip to 439 distinct names, none empty and none colliding with a hand-curated name. (private.yaml configures 446 managed entries at that instant; the 7 difference is sources that failed to fetch that cycle and so report no series to strip.) The legacy hash-only tg-96c4d7c7a7 renders as 96c4d7c7a7 and tg-inline renders as inline.

Coverage is thin, and far thinner than the hand-curated table beside it: at that same instant this job reported 439 crawler-managed sources reporting series against 45 hand-curated, so these 25 rows are a 5.7% window while the curated table's 25 cover 55.6% of its side. The crawler adds sources hourly — the figure was 327 a day earlier — so re-read the live denominator from panel 3 rather than trusting this stamp. Do NOT read the two tables side by side as a fair comparison of owners: attribution is biased AGAINST this table BY CONSTRUCTION, because config.go:985 appends the curated sources.yaml before :1000 appends the crawler's private.yaml and merge.go:79 dedupes first-wins in slice order, so on every server:port both sides supply, the curated source claims the node and this table's kept and filtered lose it. Panel 21 sums both sides and carries the same caveat.

panels.title: Top sources: hand-curated (last cycle)
panels.description:
Four counts per HAND-CURATED source (source!~"tg-.*") from the last cycle, in pipeline order, for the top 25 of that set ranked on valid — the column this table is also sorted by, so adding columns never reorders it. yielded = raw nodes the source yielded; valid = what survived the IP-stage filters, counted per source BEFORE merge dedupes across sources; kept = that source's nodes that survived the URL test, counted after merge; filtered = what then passed every through-node gate and reached the published payload. valid >= kept >= filtered holds, but the first gap is NOT probe failure alone: valid is pre-merge and kept is post-merge, so valid - kept also absorbs every node whose server:port another source supplied first (merge keeps the first label and drops the rest) plus the dead-node cache skip. That dedupe term dominates — sum(stable_source_valid_nodes) / scalar(stable_merged_nodes) ran 1.00–4.93 (avg 3.37) over the 15d window ending 2026-08-08 19:30Z, across both owners. filtered DOES attribute published nodes to a source, exactly one per node, because merge leaves one <source>-NNN label per duplicate group: a large valid with filtered 0 means nothing reached the payload under that source's own name, whether the nodes were duplicates, dead-cached, probe failures or gate drops. Note the vocabulary: kept here is THIS table's column name for the probe verdict, while the global stable_kept_nodes gauge counts what this table calls filtered. These names are shown verbatim; nothing is stripped here, unlike the crawler table, whose tg- prefix is hidden by display-only PromQL that changes no name.

Coverage here is wide, and the asymmetry against the crawler table is load-bearing: on :9091, job sub-preprocessor, 2026-08-16 12:45 +03:00 there were 45 hand-curated sources reporting series against 439 crawler-managed, so these 25 rows cover 55.6% of this side while the crawler table's 25 cover 5.7% of its own. The crawler side grows hourly, so re-read its live denominator from panel 3. The two tables are NOT comparable row for row, and this one's kept and filtered are inflated against the crawler table's BY CONSTRUCTION: config.go:985 appends the curated sources.yaml before :1000 appends the crawler's private.yaml and merge.go:79 dedupes first-wins in slice order, so on every server:port both sides supply, the curated source claims the node — this table keeps it, the crawler table loses it. The bias favours THIS table. Panel 21 sums both sides and carries the same caveat.

On the vassago instance (job sub-preprocessor-vassago) there are no tg- sources at all, so the crawler-managed table beside this one is EMPTY — all four of its targets return no series and Grafana renders "No data", not rows of zeros. There this table is the whole list: 52 curated sources reporting series at the same instant, of which the top 25 by valid are shown.

panels.title: Ownership split: crawler-managed vs hand-curated (last cycle)
panels.description: The whole list in two rows, split on who owns the source: crawler-managed (source=~"tg-.*") versus hand-curated (source!~"tg-.*"), summing the same per-source series panels 8 and 22 list one by one. That regex is the discriminator and the ONLY one available — source is the sole label on every stable_source_* series, so origin, channel and URL never reach Prometheus and there is no cleaner field to switch to. The axis is ownership, not provenance: crawl.go:36 stamps managedPrefix "tg-" on exactly the sources the crawler owns and never touches the rest, so the managed side also holds tg-inline (raw node URIs harvested out of message bodies, not a channel) and the legacy tg-<sha10> names. Columns are panel 8's, same series in the same pipeline order, plus sources = how many per-source series carry that ownership. That column counts the sources that REPORTED last cycle — it equals panel 3's stable_sources_ok, not stable_sources_total: a source that failed to fetch emits no per-source series at all, so it sits in neither row and its ownership is unknowable from Prometheus. A side with no sources on the selected instance renders no row at all rather than a zero — the selector matches nothing, so there is no series for sum to return; a single-row table here means that instance is entirely one or the other, not that the panel broke. Read filtered — stable_source_published_nodes, what reached the published payload — as ATTRIBUTION, not contribution: merge.go:79 dedupes first-wins in source order and config.go:1000 appends the crawler's private.yaml overlay AFTER the curated config/sources.yaml, so a curated source claims every node a crawler source also yields, by construction and before any quality judgement. These series cannot answer what the list would lose without the crawler; only a re-run with the overlay removed can. Nor is filtered/valid a survival rate: valid is pre-merge and double-counts a node two sources both yield, while filtered is post-attribution. Cells are live from the last cycle, so no counts are quoted here to rot.

panels.title: Cloudflare egress trace
panels.description: What the published nodes reported about themselves through Cloudflare's cdn-cgi/trace. Nothing here is a drop: a trace that fails, or one that contradicts the offline chain, still publishes the node. answered/unanswered split the published list by whether the trace completed — a large unanswered share makes the moved count below it that much less representative. moved = answered nodes whose measured egress country differs from the country the offline chain placed their resolved address in, i.e. how often the tag would have been wrong without the trace. It is a property of the pool, not a fault: an anycast front-end registers in one country and exits in another.

panels.title: Kept-node speed
panels.description: Measured download speed of the nodes published last cycle. p50/p90 are interpolated from 7 fixed buckets (5-500 Mbps); a quantile landing above the top bucket reports 500, so p90 pinned at 500 under a higher max means "faster than 500", not a plateau. max is the exact per-cycle value. Without a bandwidth filter no node has a measured speed, but the panel does NOT go blank: writeHistogram runs unconditionally and always prints _sum and _count, which are 0 and 0 over an empty slice, so the avg target's clamp_min(…, 1) evaluates 0/1 and draws a FLAT ZERO — which reads "every node is unmeasurably slow", the inverse of "not measured". Only p50/p90 (NaN over all-zero buckets) and max (its gauge is guarded by len(KeptSpeeds) > 0) actually vanish. There is deliberately no min line: the bandwidth filter drops everything below config min_mbps, so min is pinned to that floor (5–10 Mbps over the 15d window ending 2026-08-08 19:30Z, exactly 5 in 81.7% of samples) on an axis that reaches 546. stable_kept_speed_min_mbps is still exported and now renders nowhere; the actionable form of the question it was meant to answer — how many kept nodes sit ON the floor — is stable_kept_speed_mbps_bucket{le="5.0"}, which no panel on this dashboard plots either.

panels.title: Kept-node latency
panels.description: Mean probe delay of the nodes published last cycle: the value SelectSurvivors gates on with max_avg_ms and then sorts the published list by. p50/p90 are interpolated from a fixed bucket ladder that is maintained to carry a bound equal to every instance's shipped max_avg_ms — this panel is per-job, instances disagree on the threshold, and a gate falling between two bounds is exactly what the ladder exists to prevent. The tail runs past every gate only so that raising a max_avg_ms into it stays a one-file edit: SelectSurvivors drops everything above the gate, so on any job every bound at or above its threshold carries the same count as +Inf. Read p90 and max AGAINST this job's max_avg_ms: both well under it means the threshold is not the binding constraint, whereas max pressed up against it means the cut is sitting inside live population and raising it would publish more nodes. Unlike the speed panel beside it this one has no flat-zero trap: keptLatencies is unfiltered, so _count always equals stable_kept_nodes and clamp_min never binds. A cycle that publishes nothing routes to ObserveError and leaves the previous cycle's values standing; before the first published cycle the whole series is absent.

panels.title: Cycle duration, rate & failures
panels.description: Wall time of the last cycle on the left axis; cycles and failures counted over a rolling hour on the right. cycles/h counts every attempt, published or failed (stable_cycles_total HELP: "Stable cycles attempted (published + failed)"), so failures/h is a subset of it, not a parallel series. cycles/h falling to zero while the process is up is itself the alarm. TWO of these three series survive a restart with no published cycle, not all three: writeMetrics emits stable_cycles_total and stable_cycle_failures_total BEFORE its `if m.last == nil` return, so cycles/h and failures/h still say whether the worker is alive when every other panel on this dashboard reads no-data. duration is not one of them — stable_cycle_duration_seconds is a gauge written AFTER that return, so the duration line is simply absent until the first cycle publishes, and that gap is the documented cold-start state, not a scrape fault.

panels.title: Unresolved GEO tags in published list
panels.description: Published nodes whose GEO tag came out as [GEO:??] — no annotation provider resolved a country for them — as a count on the left axis and as a percentage of the published list on the right. Zero is healthy. stable_geo_unknown_nodes HELP: "Published nodes whose GEO tag is [GEO:??]: no annotation provider resolved a country." Unresolved nodes are absent from stable_kept_country_nodes, so the countries panel cannot show this: an annotation chain that collapses reads there as nothing worse than a shorter list.

panels.title: Cycle time by phase
panels.description: Where the last published cycle's wall time went, stacked. The phases come from one metric, stable_cycle_phase_duration_seconds{phase=...}, in pipeline order: fetch = every source downloaded, parsed and run through the per-node IP stage (DNS, geo/asn/cidr); merge = dedupe by server:port; dead_filter = the dead-node cache skip; probe = the whole Prober.Probe call — parsing the payload into mihomo proxies, then the TCP reachability pre-check at its own concurrency (deliberately outside check.concurrency), then the URL-test rounds, of which only the last is bounded by check.timeout * check.rounds; the pre-check is NOT broken out into a phase of its own (deferred: it would need a per-cycle plumbing path back out of Probe), so read its share off stage="condemned" on the probe-outcome panel rather than from this stack; egress = the through-node filters plus the cdn-cgi/trace measurement, each on its own timeout, which also do network work per SURVIVOR and are deliberately NOT folded into probe; publish = payload build, moved-country count, atomic swap, snapshot write and the published-cycle log line. The unstacked "cycle total" line runs ABOVE the stack on purpose: the steps between phases (dead-cache write, survivor selection, cache prune, report assembly) belong to no phase, so the gap is the cycle's own overhead and shrinking to zero is not the goal. A cycle that ABORTED contributes nothing here — ObserveError leaves the last report in place, so this stack keeps describing the last cycle that PUBLISHED, and only the failures series on the cycle-duration panel moves. Both series are absent until the first cycle publishes, the same cold-start gap the duration line has.

panels.title: Probe outcome by stage
panels.description: Where the probe ended for each node it was spent on, stacked, closed over stable_probed_nodes: condemned = the TCP reachability pre-check refused the server, so no URL test was spent on it — a saving for the cycle, never a free verdict for the node: a condemned label folds to Successes 0, recordDead blocks its server:port, and filterDead then skips that address for deadcache.ttl, 3h in both shipped configs and jittered to [3h, 4.5h), against a 1h interval — so one condemnation costs the node its next three to four cycles, which is where a yield drop on the funnel panel comes from; connect = the URL test never got a tunnel up; fetch = the tunnel came up and the GET through it failed; passed = at least one round answered, i.e. the input to SelectSurvivors. unknown is the zero ProbeStage, and it counts probed labels the prober returned NO result for — which is exactly what a node whose proxies failed adapter.ParseProxy leaves behind, since probeStages walks the probed ENTRIES and indexes the result map, so an absent label reads as the zero value instead of vanishing and the stack keeps closing over stable_probed_nodes. Non-zero here means the payload carried lines mihomo would not convert; it is not a mis-assigned stage. condemned/probed is the series to watch: it is the pre-check's yield, and it is what decides how much probe time a reachability gate can ever save — but only while stable_precheck_trusted is 1. When the pre-check's breaker discards its own verdict (trusted 0, see the TCP pre-check panel) nothing is condemned at all and this series reads 0, indistinguishable here from a pre-check that ran and found every server reachable; the endpoint counts on that panel are then the only record of the discarded verdict. An endpoint whose NAME did not resolve is not condemned either: a failed lookup proves nothing, so the pre-check fails open and the URL test decides. Measured off-prod before this shipped, 1898 TCP-gated nodes from 45 of 51 sources: 58.9% condemned, corroborated at 58.1% by an independent TCP sweep of 2861 endpoints. Do NOT expect prod to reproduce that: the measurement ran from a different egress, and it sampled the RAW merged pool while prod probes the ~26% the dead cache did not skip, a set biased toward less-dead nodes -- so prod's condemned share should be LOWER. This counts NODES, folded best-of-ports by foldProbeResults, so it cannot express what share of ATTEMPTS burned the full check.timeout; that is an attempt statistic and no series here reproduces it. An aborted cycle contributes nothing: ObserveError leaves the last report in place, so the stack keeps describing the last cycle that PUBLISHED.

panels.title: Top countries in published list (last cycle)
panels.description: At most 15 countries: the ones contributing most to the published list, last cycle. topk(15) returns one bar per country that HAS nodes, so a collapsed cycle shows fewer — over the 15d window ending 2026-08-08 19:30Z the resolved-country count was under 15 for 1668 of 20578 sample-minutes and bottomed at 3. Bar colour is scaled to the largest bar on the panel (min 0), so it encodes share of the top country and nothing else: no colour on this panel means "bad". Thresholds cannot leak into that. A continuous palette derives a bar's colour purely from its percent of the panel maximum and ignores the threshold step outright, so the green-base/red-from-80 set Grafana merges into every panel that declares none of its own — this one included — is inert here. The palette is deliberately not a green-yellow-red one all the same: a no-value display is coloured at percent 0, the LOW end of whatever scale the panel carries, and for green-yellow-red that is GREEN, an empty panel painted healthy. Blue-purple's low end asserts nothing. Nodes no provider could place are not in this metric at all; they are the [GEO:??] count on the panel to the left.

panels.title: IP-stage drops by reason
panels.description: Nodes the per-node filters dropped in preprocess, summed over every source and split by reason. dns = the server name resolved to nothing; ipv6 = the server is an IPv6 literal, which this pipeline refuses before any lookup; geo = the country allow-list; asn = the ASN deny-patterns; cidr = the CIDR allow-list, the resolved IP falling outside every configured range, dropped in preprocess before any probe; geoblock = the host is in the geoblock store the through-node gemini/claude/chatgpt checks populate. unsupported is the odd one out and is not a filter drop at all: it counts input lines containing "://" that did not parse as a node — a truncated body, a corrupt vmess payload, an HTML error page — so it is a source going bad, and it is deliberately outside the fetched total on the yield panel. ALL SEVEN ARE EMITTED EVERY CYCLE whether or not a filter behind them is configured: writeSources builds a fixed seven-entry table per source and never consults the filter list. But only geo, asn and cidr are GATED by `filters:` — geo needs a `- type: country` with a non-empty exclude set (GeofeedFilter returns early when the allow set is full and the deny set empty) or a `- type: asn` whose ASN-resolved country the policy rejects; asn needs that same entry's name-deny patterns; cidr needs a `- type: cidr` entry with a non-empty `urls:`, the only thing IPFilterSpecs turns into a CIDR spec. So a zero is ambiguous on those three only, between filter-absent, filter-configured-with-an-empty-exclude-list and filter-configured-and-broken, and the authority on which is the config THE SELECTED JOB'S INSTANCE LOADS — `config/config.yaml` for job="sub-preprocessor", `config-vassago/config.yaml` for job="sub-preprocessor-vassago", each bind-mounted at /config by docker-compose. Read that file's `filters:` list, because the two instances run DIFFERENT chains: a reason that is a flat zero under one job can be the dominant series under the other, and neither instance answers for the other. The other four are unconditional pipeline behaviour that no `filters:` entry can switch off — geoblock fires whenever the geoblock store is open (the separate `geoblock:` block), ipv6 and dns fire inside processNode straight off resolveNode, and unsupported is counted by the parser before any filter exists — so on those four a zero does mean the pipeline looked and found nothing. All seven every cycle holds for the CURRENT build, not for every sample behind it: reason="ipv6" was only added to that table on 2026-07-29 and reason="cidr" is newer still, landing with this branch, and each series begins at the selected job's first published cycle on a build carrying it — not the same instant on both jobs — so a range reaching back past that point plots fewer series over its early span: five before ipv6, six before cidr, seven only after both. Worker cycle only: the on-demand GET / path runs the same IP-stage chain but reports no metrics.

panels.title: IP-stage yield
panels.description: Raw nodes every source yielded against what reached the merge step, plus the survival percentage on the right axis. Both are summed per source and counted before dedupe, so "survived IP-stage" normally sits well above merged nodes on the funnel — 119159 against 33737 in the cycle published 2026-08-08 17:29Z. Its floor is equality, not a margin: the ratio to merged hit exactly 1.00 for 81 minutes of the 15d window ending 2026-08-08 19:30Z — the same 81 in which a source outage held ok at 1 on the sources tile, when a single source supplied every node and there was nothing left to dedupe across sources. "fetched" excludes input lines the parser refused: those are counted as reason=unsupported on the drops panel to the left and are deliberately not in this total, so the two panels do not add up and are not meant to.

panels.title: TCP pre-check (reachability)
panels.description: What the TCP reachability pre-check inside the probe phase did, in ENDPOINTS: one distinct server:port is dialled once, so a multi-port mierus:// node counts several times here, and a node whose adapter reaches its server over UDP (hysteria2/tuic/mieru, or vless xhttp-over-QUIC) is dialled not at all — no line here is the condemned NODE count on "Probe outcome by stage". Three states, which must never be read alike. verdict trusted = 1: the verdict was used, and every refused endpoint was condemned unprobed and dead-cached for deadcache.ttl. verdict trusted = 0: the breaker rejected it — refused at least 95% of the endpoints it JUDGED, a signature of a local egress fault or a degenerate check.timeout rather than a dead pool; a resolver outage does not reach this breaker at all, since an unresolvable endpoint is judged by nobody and counted as unresolved — so the verdict was DISCARDED and every node was URL-tested; stage="condemned" then reads 0 exactly as it does for a pre-check that ran and condemned nobody, and "refused" here is the only surviving trace of what was thrown away. No series at all: no pre-check ran in the last published cycle (a prober without one, or nothing published or scraped yet). refused ~59% of dialled is the healthy band measured on this pool. unresolved is the DNS fail-open share, ~5%: the name never became an address inside the dial budget, which proves nothing about the endpoint, so those nodes were probed instead of condemned — a spike there is a resolver fault, not a pool fault.
